# Pettifer

## Overview

- **Age:** Middle-aged to advanced years  <sub>[v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v2 c1 P3](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0003), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- **Origin:** Scottsford, New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer and mail carrier  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007), [v3 c18 P24](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0024)</sub>
- **Titles:** Mr.  <sub>[v2 c1 P3](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0003)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Pettifer is low in stature, heavy-set, and bald. He has a circular countenance and bulging blue eyes. When in a bad temper, his face turns violet, though he is customarily seen around his farm smoking a pipe.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c6 P56](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0056)_

## Personality

Distinct and eccentric, Mr. Pettifer is known for his extreme candor, impetuosity, and tendency to voice his exact thoughts without filter. Though he can be critical, exacting, and quick to anger, he is fundamentally friendly and supportive to those he likes. He resents being pitied, holds strong opinions about literature, and harbors a deep dislike for hypocrisy and overly rigid morality.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c17 P78](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0078), [v2 c20 P8](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0008), [v3 c11 P50](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0050), [v3 c12 P41](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0041), [v3 c12 P72](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0072)_

## History

After relocating from Scottsford, New Brunswick to Brierley, Mr. J. A. Pettifer purchased the Bell farm. He quickly gained a reputation as an eccentric bachelor, maintaining an irregular household with his hired helper John Henry Carter and his parrot Nutmeg. Initial encounters with his neighbor Nell Abernethy were turbulent due to a runaway cow, but the two soon formed a warm, lasting friendship. Rumors briefly circulated that he was courting Isabella Pullen, though he was merely visiting Gorham Pullen for business and playing checkers with Mr. Pettifer Pullen. It was later revealed that he had previously married Emily Scott in fulfillment of a deathbed promise to his sister; after a period of marital conflict over her constant housecleaning and her dislike of Nutmeg, Emily reunited with him in Brierley. In addition to farming, he took up delivering the mail and offered critical yet encouraging feedback on Nell's early literary manuscripts.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P3](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0003), [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c4 P28](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0028), [v2 c17 P76](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0076), [v2 c24 P5](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0005), [v2 c25 P47](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0047), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v3 c11 P50](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0050), [v3 c12 P41](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0041), [v3 c12 P72](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0072), [v3 c18 P24](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0024)_

## Background by volume

- Was routinely flogged by his schoolmaster as a boy  <sub>[v2 c4 P36](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0036)</sub>
- Formerly lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick, where his late sister managed his home  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Promised his dying sister he would propose to Emily Scott  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Received his foul-mouthed parrot, Nutmeg, from his late seafaring brother  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Was a lifelong bachelor before his eventual marriage  <sub>[v2 c17 P77](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0077), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>

## Quotes

> Ignore that parrot. He . . . he utters foolishness constantly. My brother, a seafaring man, gave him to me. A sailor's speech isn't always particularly refined, and birds like parrots copy things easily.  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006)</sub>

> On occasion, I am overly impetuous myself, miss . . . much too impetuous. However, I am unable to refrain from voicing my exact thoughts, and people are required to accept me as I am.  <sub>[v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023)</sub>

> That old bother Agatha Sowerby dropped by once more today, nagging me to contribute money for purchasing a vestry room carpet. My hatred for that woman exceeds my feelings for anyone else I am acquainted with.  <sub>[v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000)</sub>

> Well, I imagine you will continue to write them  <sub>[v3 c12 P72](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0072)</sub>

> Once you have finished Wexcombe, it will be time for you to find a husband. I do not believe in delaying marriage for too long—as I did.  <sub>[v3 c12 P76](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0076)</sub>
